3. The case of plaintiffs is that, suit land originally belongs to Bhawal Raj. The suit land of schedule 'Ka' comprising of an area of 23.13 acres of land recorded in CS khatian No. 7 along with other lands in the name of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Chowdhury settled the suit land in raiyati right. On the death of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, his heirs as of tenanted right was owner in possession of the entire land of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As per Court of Wards Act 1879, the management and administration of the property including "Ka" schedule land of CS khatian No.  7 was taken over by the Court of Wards. During the last CS record, it was recorded in the name of Court of Wards, for Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others, which was subsequently named as Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate or Bhawal Court of Wards Estate or Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate. Bhawal Court of Wards Estate as owner and possessor of `Ka' schedule land with other lands of CS khatian No.  7, settled 'Ka' schedule land with the father and husband of the plaintiff. Bashoruddin and co-sharer, Chand Mia through its own printed pattannama. Basiruddin and Chand Mia became owner and possessor in equal share. While Basiruddin and Chand Mia on the basis of pattannama and dakhila and by paying zamindari taxes to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate, the Government, then province of East Pakistan by giving effect of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act acquired the rent receiving interest of the Zaminder and on taking nominal taxes as land development tax, the tenants were classified as owner of their respective land as per sections 3 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After acquisition of the rent receiving interest as aforesaid, Government published final gazette as per provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act on 24-3-1952. After acquisition of the land as aforesaid, Compensation Assessment Roll were prepared and Zaminder as per the aforesaid compensation assessment roll received compensation and gazette was published on 29-5-1956 as per section 42 of the aforesaid Act by which the Zamindari of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury of `Ka' schedule land, was acquired and the status of tenant. Basiruddin and Chand Mia were changed and become owners. Accordingly SA khatian was finally published in their names. By opening jote in the revenue office and by paying nominal land development tax possessing the suit land SA khatian No.  63 was finally published in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia in equal 8 annas share. Basiruddin and Chand Mia upon an amicable settlement partitioned the kha schedule land by which 'Ka' schedule land fallen in the saham of Basiruddin. After acquisition of the land by the Government, 5.40 acres of land remain in the hand of Basiruddin alone which has been mentioned in 'Kha' schedule. Chand Mia got 'Ga' schedule land which comprising of 0.39 acres of land of dag No. 155/1061, 0.51 acres of land of dag No. 1059, 1.42 acres of land of dag No. 1063, 1.18 acres of land of dag No. 1058, 0.60 acres of land of dag No. 1060, in total, 4.10 acres of land and remaining land, in total 13.36 acres including 12.5 as mentioned in 'Gha' schedule was in ejmlali and co-sharers as owners owned and possessed by cultivation. While the aforesaid land was in possession of co-sharers, 1.48 acres of land was acquired by the Government out of 13.63 acres of land for road and remaining land i.e. 12.15 acres of land, "Gha' schedule, was in ejmali of the co-sharers. While co-sharers as aforesaid was in possession having title there to, Government acquired portion of land for defendant No. 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, defendant No. 17, Rice Research Institution from the land of Chand Mia to the very knowledge of defendant No.  1 and 14 in LA Case No.  100/65-66, recognizing Chand Mia as the owner of the aforesaid land. Compensation was received by Chand Mia while in possession, 12.15 acres of land described in schedule `Gha', constructed homestead, planted trees and cultivated agricultural lands in ejmali, died leaving, defendant No.  6 as heir who along with other co-sharers possessing the land in ejmali. While defendant No. 6, plaintiff and Chand Mia was in possession of the ejmali property of 'Gha' schedule comprising 12.15 acres, Government in LA case No.  5/85-86 acquired 10 acres of land for defendant No.  19, Gazipur District Police Line under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs. In LA Case No.  3/2001-2002 Government acquired 0.33 acres of land for defendant No.  26, District Fisheries Officer under defendant No.  25, Ministry of Fisheries and Veterinaries under Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  7/90-91 acquired 0.09 acres of land for defendant No. 20, District Jail, Gazipur under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs, in LA Case No.  3/95-96 acquired 0.33 acres of land for Defendant No.  District primary Education office under defendant No. 21 Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  5/90-91 acquired .50 acres of land for defendant No.  24, Public Health Engineering Department under defendant No.  23, Ministry of Health, Government of Bangladesh. Government disbursed compensation money part of the afore-said 5 LA cases to the plaintiffs and to the co-sharers having found they are legal title holder. Some greedy person of the locality created obstruction in getting compensation money and gave proposal to defendant No. 6, son of defendant No. 9 and brother of defendant Nos.  1 and 8, but recognized their title over 'Kha' schedule land when they would manage in getting the compensation money to the plaintiffs. Later on, Chand Mia died leaving defendant Nos.  2-5 as heirs. Plaintiffs, the heirs of Chand Mia, defendant Nos. 2-5 are waiting for getting compensation money. Suddenly, on 12-12-2007 the manager of defendant No. 14 and the officer of Bhawal Court of Wards came to 'Kha' schedule land whereupon plaintiff could know that defendant No. 1 of the instant suit along with defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 filed in the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur against defendant Nos. 3-6, in total against 11 persons as defendants and they got decree. Defendant No. 1 of the instant suit got decree up to the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. In RS record 18.70 acres of land of 'Kha' schedule recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 and they requested plaintiffs to give up possession of the suit land. Defendant No.  1 of the instant suit threatened plaintiff that if they did not give up possession to the defendant No.  14 amicably then they by force evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land. Plaintiffs went to defendant No.  14 to know about the decree, then, the manager of defendant No.  14, Abdur Rouf, gave a paper book to plaintiff No.  1 and requested plaintiff No.  1 to go through paper book to find out how the suit was decreed. Plaintiffs after getting paper book asked defendant Nos.  6 and 3 as to how they got decree in the suit to which they kept silence. Defendant No. 1 with connivance with defendant Nos.  6-13 got the decree surreptitiously. 

 4. It is further case of plaintiffs that defendant No. 1 was never owner and possessor of the suit land from defendant No.  14 in any manner either as tenant or as Raiyat. The lands upon which defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho claimed title Extinguished from the moment State Acquisition of Tenancy Act published in gazette on 24-3-1952 and vested in the Government, as such, defendant No. 1 looses his right to collect rent from the plaintiffs or any-body. 

 5. It is further case of plaintiffs that, defendant Nos.  1 to 14 in connivance with the employees of Deputy Commissioner turned the relevant portions of SA khatian which was kept in the record room of Deputy Commissioner but the said SA khatian having been kept in other offices like tahsil, AC Land office including DG, DLR office of the Government wherein the said SA khatian with index is found and on scrutinizing of SA khatian No.  63 it appears that said SA khatian No.  63 was prepared in the name of predecessor of Basiruddin and Chand Mia and on the basis of said SA record the other document i.e. for collection of the rent, i.e. talab baki register which is retisger-2 and from Union land office, earlier Tohsil Office it is seen the record stand, in the name of plaintiffs predecessor and in index in different LA Cases, wherein on the basis of said SA khatian No.  63, lands were acquired and compensation money were disbursed in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. It is seen that the aforesaid khatian was prepared in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. 

 11. The case of defendant No.  6 is that this defendant has no claim over 'Kha' schedule land. While his predecessor, Chand Mia was alive out of an amicable partition 'Ka' schedule land was fallen in the share of Chand Mia and since then this defendant possessing 'Ka' schedule land. This defendant never appeared in any of the suit including Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 as the name of father of this defendant has been written as Rashid Uddin and Ashraf Ali of that suit, is a different person, not this defendant and by that decree title of this defendant cannot extinguish. 

 17. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff appellants, submits that, pattannama exhibit-2 was disbelieved by the learned Judge on the ground that dates mentioned therein in Bengali has no similarity with the corresponding English date without properly going through the contents thereof as the date in Bengali mentioned in the middle side of the pattannama is the preliminary date of pattan subject to the approval of the Chief Manager and the date in English after signature of the concerned Nayeb of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate is the date after approval of the pattan by the Chief Manager of the said Court of Wards. Learned Advocate further submits that judgment passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and also of those of the higher Courts up to the Appellate Division wherein decision arrived are not supported by law as the lands of SA Khaian No.  63 of the suit land was settled as pr6jabili and as per President Order No. 90 of 1972 no suit can be filed against the lands settled as projabili as such said judgment having passed on wrong assumption of law affirmed up to Appellate Division is a judgment per in curium. Learned Advocate submits that rent receipts were granted by the Zaminder and thereafter, by the Revenue Authority of the Government after whole sale acquisition of the land and on the face of such legal position, preparation of RS khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 is without any basis, the court below without considering the materials on record abruptly hold pattanana as forged which finding is erroneous in as much as the names of Basiruddin and Chand Mia was duly recorded in the subsequent documents like Register II, the Talab Baki Register, exhibit-5, Compensation Assessment Roll, exhibit-8, rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit-4 and lastly in SA khatian, record of right after effecting the 'projapattani'. Learned Advocate further submits that document filed connecting with projapattani being more than 30 years old and has been produced from proper custody of the plaintiff-appellants got presumptive value of its execution and further submits that learned Judge committed gross illegality in holding that SA khatian produced form, the side of plaintiffs is a created document upon using a revenue stamp and bears no signature of Officer-in-Charge of record room is baseless and against the record and also against order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 passed by the learned Judge on the application filed by the plaintiffs for calling the record from the Revenue Department whereupon the court ordered that since Government produced SA khatian as such record from Revenue Department is not required to be called to settle the dispute without considering that Government produced distorted SA khatian. Learned Advocate further submits that the findings of the learned Judge that in Title Suit No. 12 of 1976 it is decided Chand Mia is a bargadar under defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is baseless and fully on surmise and conjecture as the contesting defendant-respondent No. 1 and 14 who claimed their title through those judgments, had neither filed nor exhibited those judgment in the present suit as such finding of the learned Judge that Chand Mia had admitted in those previous suits that he was a bargadar is baseless and full of surmise and conjecture not supported by any law. Learned Advocate further submits that court below was in erroneous findings of fact as it should have considered the vital documents like the rent receiving interest acquisition gazettes, exhibit Nos. 7 and 9, written statements of defendant Nos.  6 to 32, true copy of the SA khatian produced by the Government, exhibit No.  `Kha; the register No. II i.e. Talab Baki Register, exhibit No. 5, Compensation Assessment Roll exhibit No. 8 and the rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit No. 4, which are although in certified copies are not challenged by the Government while marked as exhibits and non-consideration of those vital documents led the Court below to erroneous finding as to the title of the plaintiffs-appellants. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs-appellants from the time of pattan upto the date of forceful eviction on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 has been proved by the oral and documentary evidences of the plaintiffs-appellants and also by the defendant's witnesses, DW 1 and DW 2, learned Judge committed gross illegality in not declaring title of the plaintiffs over the suit property by adverse possession. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs have been proved through municipal tax receipts, electric and gas bills, house rent receipts etc. exhibit 13 series and also Advocate Commissioner's report and such non-consideration of those vital documents as to possession of the plaintiffs led the Court to an erroneous finding as to title of the plaintiffs, as possession follows title. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No.  1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho having not been represented by the Shebayet in the previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 2985 as plaintiff and in the subsequent present Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  14 the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate having no connection with the deity, has no locus standi to file the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 and also to contest the subsequent Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as its representative, so, the decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and the dismissal decree passed in Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 is illegal and without jurisdiction. Learned Advocate further submits that neither defendant No. 1 nor defendant No.  14 filed any document of acquiring title in the suit property nor proved their possession therein, but the learned trial court dismissed the suit on coming to the conclusion on surmise that the defendant No. 1 is a owner of the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 14 having admitted that all the properties except ‘Kha' schedule property have been acquired by the Government and also compensation have been paid to the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 for recovery of khas possession of the entire 18.73 acres of land including the acquired land, is illegal and not binding upon the persons in possession through acquisition. 

 18. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate in support of his submissions, on wholesale acquisition and on rent receipts, relied on the case of reported in 27 DLR (AD) 109, 2 MLR (AD) 156 = 2 BLC (AD) 129, 33 DLR (AD) 13, 33 DLR (AD) 52, 14 MLR (AD) 401, 13 MLR (AD) 329, 13 MLR (AD) 353, 24 BLD (AD) 43, 32 DLR 252, 8 BLD 497, 9 MLR (AD) 82, 60 DLR (AD) 24,15 MLR (AD) 89, 35 DLR (AD) 42. We will consider the decisions if required later on. 

 23. Facts of the case relates to hated system called 'Zamindari invented by Britishers for protecting the British Raj. The zaminders stood against Independent movement lest they lost their position. To protect the zaminders section 19A of the Arms Act was inserted. These zaminders had no character excepting adulate, glorify and flatter obsequiously Britishers. These Zaminders for pleasing their masters, (Britishers) did everything. They realize taxes from subjects, particularly from Muslim, mercilessly. Among the Zamindars, Rabindra Nath Tagore is well known to us. Person is known how he react when his/her selfish self-interest is in challenge. He for oppressing his Muslim subjects for realising rents brought 1st time in Bengal, 'Beharies'. He tooth and nail objected to installation of Dhaka University so that his subjects, Muslims may not get light of education. For his leadership, division of Bangla was annulled. He came to Dhaka and berthed his 'Bazra' in river Buriganga, opposite to famous Gangazali and wrote "Banglar Badhu buke tar madhu" but he did not hear the sound of ' Azan' nor saw the moon of Bid and other muslim festivals.  32. The expression "Projabili" as used in this kabuliat was held to include the grant of permanent tenure. With great respect to Mr justice Das, We must observe that he was not quite correct in distinguishing the case of Afazuddi (B) (39 Cal 138) on the ground that what was held to be a protected interest in that case was a non-occupancy right. The facts of that case will show that one Prasanna Kumar Mitra created a permanent tenure in favour of Bhojendra Kumar Sen who in his turn granted a permanent tenure in favour of Bahojendra Kumar Sen who in his turn granted a permanent lease to one Ganesh Chandra Chatterjee and Ganesh Chandra Chatterjee created a raiyati lease in favour of the plaintiff. The tenancy of Bhojendra was sold in execution of a decree for arrears of rent and the purchaser at the rent sale sought to annul the interest of Ganesh and also of the plaintiff. Jenkins CJ and D Chatterjee J held that the interest of Ganesh was protected and therefore the interest of the plaintiff could not be touched. 

 33. It was clearly held in this case that the permanent tenure in favour of Ganesh was included in the expression "Projabili" which occurred in the head lease and therefore the interest of Ganesh was protected under cl. (g) of section 160, Bengal Tenancy Act, Unfortunately the earlier decision in the case of - "11 Cal LJ 87 (A), was brought to the notice of the learned Judges in 'Afazuddi's case, (B)' with the result that the expression " Projabili" was held to include the creation of a tenure in the latter case, while the decision in the former case was to the contrary. In the case before us, however, the recital in the head lease (Exhibit A) is somewhat different from the recitals in the leases in the two cases discussed above. In this case the expression "projabili" is placed in juxtaposition to the word "Nijakarkite" (cultivation by the lessee himself) and is an alternative to khas cultivation. From these facts it is reasonable to conclude that the expression "Projabili" in Exhibit 'A' means settlement with cultivating raiyats only. 

 42. Plaintiffs case is that they got pattern of the land from Zaminder of Bhawal and since then they are in possession, at first, under the Zaminder and later on, under the Government until dispossess in 2008. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 2 is that property having belongs to a deity, this property could not be alienated by anyone except legal necessity; RS khatian prepared rightly, plaintiffs title has been extinguished and defendant No. 1 having got decree in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 this suit was dismissed rightly. The case of defendant No.  6 is that he was not a party to Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 as he did not appeared in the suit and his father's name was not rightly recorded. It is the case of defendant No.  6 that defendant No. 1 had no title nor possession and on the basis of decree of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 defendant Nos.  1 and 14 illegally threatened plaintiffs from dispossession from the suit land. Defendant Nos.  6-17 wants saham for 4.10 acres of land which has been acquired for Bangladesh Rice Research Institute. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that the suit land has been acquired from plaintiffs by different LA Cases and suit land has been rightly recorded in the name of plaintiffs and SA, khatian No. 63 in 8 annas equal share to Basiruddin, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, predecessor of the defendant Nos.  2 and 6. 

 43. It appears that Government in written statement admitted plaintiffs are the owner of the suit property as in the written statement Government stated that in different LA Cases Government acquired land from plaintiffs and from their co-sharer and SA Khatian No.  63 was rightly prepared in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and also of his co-sharer, Chand Mia and it is also the case of the Government that plaintiff of Title Suit No 1219 of 1985 and defendant No.  1 of the instant suit has no title or possession. As such, title of the plaintiffs has well established. On this background let us refer to the depositions of the witnesses particularly of defendant's witnesses who stated as:— 

 47. We have scrutinized this document. In the pattannama there is a statement to the effect that “ ম্যানেজার সাহেব মঞ্জুর না করিলে বন্দোবস্ত আমলে আসিবে না। ইতি ১৩৪৫ সনের ২৯ শে বৈশাখ।” this pattan requires to be approved by the manager. Pattannama was approved on 25-5-1938. So this deed speaks of proposal and approval as such, there is two different dates as proposal and approval cannot be given on the same date. The learned Judge totally misread this exhibit-2, basic documents of title of plaintiffs as it has a legal force. For non-production of this exhibit in the earlier suit the title of plaintiff cannot extinguish. It may be said that the earlier suit was not properly conducted. In the earlier suit President Order No.  90 of 1972 was not also considered as the suit was filed by Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho. 

 48. This pattannama has been acted upon as from exhibit-3 series it appears that the pat-tan holder paid Zaminderi tax up to 1942 then from exhibit No. 4, dakhila, it appears land has been recorded as 'projabili' extinguishing title of Superior landlord, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. From exhibit No.  2-4 it appears from the column of the khatian that name of plaintiffs and co-sharer have been recorded for 23.13 acres of land as projabili. Exhibt-5 is Talib Baki Register-II kept in the custody of Government where also we find the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs from whom tax was collected. Exhibit-6 series are rent receipts stand in the name of plaintiffs and their predecessor. Up to this plaintiffs have been able to prove that they have paid rent to the Zaminder pursuant to the pattan taken from Zaminder i.e. up to 1952. 

 "No.  2773 LR -26th February 1952. In exercise of the power by sub-section (f) of section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), it is hereby notified, for the information of all concerned, that the 'Governor is pleased to acquire, with effect from the 14th April, all interests of the rent-receivers named in column 1 of the schedule below in the estates and taluks and tenures, the particulars whereof are given in column 2 of the schedule against their names including all their interests in all such-soil and rights to minerals in such estates and taluks and tenures." 

 51. So, after promulgation of the gazette in 1952, March, 24, Zamindari system having been abolished the plaintiffs predecessor became land owner. Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act speaks that rents receiving interest has been devolved upon the Government not upon the Zaminder. Exhibit-7, a copy of Dhaka gazette wherein the suit land has been included. Exhibit-8, compensation assessment roll shows that some lands were acquired by the Government from the predecessor of the plaintiffs taking them as 'Malik' of the suit land as projabili. Exhibit-9 also a copy of Dhaka Gazette, the last gazette published under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act includes the suit land as:— 

 "Under the provision of sub-section (2) of section 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), read with section 46 C of the said Act, the Governor is pleased to declare that Compensation Assessment-rolls in respect of such properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in the Schedule below as have been acquire under section 3 or will be deemed to be acquired under clause (3) of section 46 E of that Act, have been finally published under section 42 of the said Act on the date shown against each." 

 56. After promulgation of Bangladesh Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No.  IX of 1976), new law under section 2(A) inserted i.e. the power of the Court of Wards vested in the Divisional Commissioner of respective areas. By the Bangladesh law, Board of Land Administration of the Government took place in place of Court of Wards, after acquisition of rent receiving interest of the concerned estate the tenants of the Bhawal Raj Estate were no more tenants under them and became "Malik" directly under the Government. Management of the properties of disqualified owners by the Court of Wards is a matter of long past. Either they have overcome their disqualification in the meantime or have died leaving heirs to inherit the estates. Alter publication of general notification No.  2773 dated 26-2-52, exhibit-7, under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the notification No.  3126 dated 27-2-56, exhibit-11, declaring the Compensation Assessment-rolls under section 43(2) read with section 46 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all rent receiving interest stood acquired and the tenants of any such rent receivers became "Malik" directly under the Government and all non-retainable khas land vested in the Government. 

 "It is to be further observed that it is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs the Province of East Pakistan: (1967) 19 DLR 106 decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiki vs the Province of East Pakistan (1968) 20 DLR (SC) 144 PLD 1968 SC 185 that on the publication of the notification under section 3 of the Act, all rent receiving interests including that of Debuttor and Waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government." In paragraph 4 of the judgment, it is held: "There is another fact which needs to be noted that in the year 1963 notifications under section 43 of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquiring of all interests other than already acquired under section 3 of the Act completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act. All the notifications have been published in the Official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact that requires to be noted is that President's Order No. 90 of 1972, the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) (Third) Order 1972, was promulgated on 3rd August, 1972 long after the observation made in some of the decisions of the High Court, Dacca on the retention by the Mutwalli or Shebait of an estate on account of non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment made in President' Order No.  90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, appeals, applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act No.  XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance 1956 (EB Ordinance No III of 1956) or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all order, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suit, appeals applications and other legal Proceeding shall cease to have any effect; and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

 60. On a reading the plaint, written statement and depositions of the witnesses it appears that the Bigraho is a private one, not a public one. Defendant No.  1 did not produce any deed, i.e. endowment, by which it can be said the Bigraho was a public one and also can be seen that no shebayet and no pujari, either represent the Bigraho or deposed to prove the fact that any of the family member of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury live in any part of Bangladesh or to prove the fact that the Bigraho is still functioning, no witness come from the side of defendant No.  1 to prove any one of Hindu community worshiping the Bigraho. In installation of Deity there must be an endeavor or endowment by a deed. Defendant No.  1 in support of their case did not produce any document or evidence to show the deity is still existence after leaving of Zaminders to Calcutta in 1919. It is evidenced that Bigraho is a family one. In Hindu Law, two categories of deity, one is family deity or private and another is public deity. If it is public deity the properties of the deity cannot be alienated but if it is private deity of a family it move with family. No such deed produce from the side of defendant No. 1 to show dedication was for public. Moreover, there are some other feature to be looked into i.e. who bears the cost of festivity and Raj Bhog of said deity and also there be positive assertion of delivery of possession of moveable and immoveable property to deity. There are also two other important feature to hold a deity a public one i.e. first, payment of public demand and second, salaries to the different employees of deity. 

 64. From the side of defendant No. 1 it appears that attested copy of SA khatian No.  63 was produced exhibit 'Ka' and RS khatian No.  506. Learned Judge disbelieved SA khatian exhibit 1 submitted by plaintiff as it is not tallied with the certified copy of the SA khatian produced from the side of defendant No.  1. We are of the view that learned Judge was totally on wrong premises as plaintiff not only produced certified copy but also in their statement stated that this SA khatian can be found from different departments of government and also from the Government and filed application for calling for the volume from concern Assistant Commissioner (land) of Gazipur whereupon the court passed order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 as:— 

 67. Exhibits 7 and 9 published under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with reference to particular estates, taluks, tenures, holding and tenancies and in respect of all rent receivers whose properties were under the management of Court of Wards Act, 1876. Sub-section 2(a) was enacted and introduced in section 3 of the Act by ordinance No.  111 of 1956. After this amendment, by general notification dated 2nd April, 1956 issued district wise in regard to all rent receiving interest which thereafter vested in the Government with effect from 14-4-56 in terms of those notification. As such, after 14-4-56 the defendant No.  1 has no right, title, interest or possession in itself what-ever it has, gone under the Government, not of it in any individual form to initiate any proceeding.
